observedIssues.fact: All nine platform examples placed a block HTML marker between rows 4 and 5, which ended the GitHub Markdown table.
observedIssues.decision: Move the marker before the table and enforce one consecutive header, separator, and seven-row block.
observedIssues.resolution: All nine files are corrected and covered by comment, blank-line, row-count, and marker-position mutations.
observedIssues.followUp: Complete PR, Hosted CI, merge, closure, and branch cleanup.

observedIssues.fact: The three guides had ten-stage explanation and a final success list but no independently fillable complete calibration checklist.
observedIssues.decision: Add a distinct ten-row, seven-field checklist to every language and compare stable stage IDs.
observedIssues.resolution: English, Chinese, and Japanese now each record state, evidence, answer, Candidate, Owner/Reviewer, and PASS/STOP for all ten stages.
observedIssues.followUp: Complete PR, Hosted CI, merge, closure, and branch cleanup.

observedIssues.fact: The previous prompt treated moving main/release.json as release evidence; current main metadata does not match the published v0.5.42 asset digest, and newer v0.5.44 and v0.5.43 tag-pinned metadata still declare v0.5.42, so latest-published is not equivalent to latest-verifiable.
observedIssues.decision: Do not hardcode a replacement version or silently downgrade. Inspect stable releases newest-to-oldest, require the provider record, tag-pinned metadata, installer, archive, and digests to agree, and STOP for explicit user direction before using an older verifiable release.
observedIssues.resolution: All three guides now exclude draft/prerelease and moving-main digest authority, select the highest verifiable evidence chain, and require explicit STOP before older fallback; mutations reject moving-main and hardcoded semantic versions.
observedIssues.followUp: Fix the published release metadata production defect before the later release Work Item; complete this documentation lifecycle first.

observedIssues.fact: The first checklist draft told beginners to copy Markdown into validated Summary JSON, used yes/no where the Session requires yes_no, and omitted a bounded activation procedure.
observedIssues.decision: Use the persisted Calibration Session as authority, map human labels to exact machine values, and separate read-only activation planning from bounded approval.
observedIssues.resolution: Three-language prompts now locate and operate the Session for the user, require manual unknown-as-STOP under the current runtime limitation, and show bounded activation/recovery evidence.
observedIssues.followUp: Re-run independent documentation review and full lifecycle verification.

observedIssues.fact: Japanese iOS, Android, and Java guides contained useful seven-stage filled-answer examples that were absent from English and Chinese, and Stage 7 did not require concrete per-requirement evidence tables.
observedIssues.decision: Preserve the stronger Japanese content, add semantically aligned English and Chinese examples, and require evidence path/URL, commit SHA, PASS/STOP, missing item, and platform identity in Stage 7.
observedIssues.resolution: All nine platform guides now have an uninterrupted abstract seven-stage request table plus an uninterrupted seven-stage filled example; the checker and mutation test enforce the example.
observedIssues.followUp: Confirm semantic parity in the final five-strategy documentation review and Hosted rendering.

observedIssues.fact: Published tags v0.5.44 and v0.5.43 carry tag-pinned metadata that declares v0.5.42, while only the older v0.5.42 metadata and asset digest agree; choosing the newest tag would be unverifiable.
observedIssues.decision: Document dynamic highest-verifiable selection and an explicit STOP before an older fallback, without fixing the procedure to any version.
observedIssues.resolution: Three-language discovery prompts and a stable boundary marker now encode the non-silent-fallback rule.
observedIssues.followUp: The later release prerequisite must correct release metadata generation and published evidence before releasing.

observedIssues.fact: Final Accuracy and Completeness review found that archive verification was described as installer input, plain Make targets were used despite Wizard-default integration off, yes_no was called a value, display labels were called machine IDs, phase records were treated as actor identity, Stage 10 ordering was circular, full checklist persistence was overclaimed, Active/Session persistence was overclaimed as one atomic transaction, and fallback/mode/CI/Unknown recovery paths were incomplete.
observedIssues.decision: Align all three guides with install.sh, Makefile.ai, ai_install_wizard.py, and ai_calibrate.py; add bounded fallback, mode routing, explicit Makefile.ai invocation, exact answer type/value, external actor evidence, correct Stage 10 ordering, schema-supported evidence locations, Active-file-only atomicity, CI-gap closure, and STOP/retry examples.
observedIssues.resolution: The three guides and nine examples now state the executable paths and limitations accurately; stable boundary markers and mutations reject recurrence, including Session persistence and Active/Session atomicity drift.
observedIssues.followUp: Run final independent review and complete Hosted lifecycle evidence.

observedIssues.fact: quality-fast failed because the documentation Make-target invariant understood only no-argument options such as -n, treated -f and the uppercase TARGET placeholder as real targets, and therefore could not represent the required Makefile.ai adopter entrypoint.
observedIssues.decision: Extend the parser red-first to consume -f/--file plus its filename before validating the actual target, use explicit <target> placeholders, and keep novice steps prompt-first with a conditional installed entrypoint.
observedIssues.resolution: Focused invariant regressions pass, the system invariant accepts make -f Makefile.ai quality-fast, and the three guides no longer present unconditional plain-make commands.
observedIssues.followUp: Re-run quality-fast, final documentation review, and the full governed lifecycle.

observedIssues.fact: scripts/ai_calibrate.py currently records an unknown answer as a complete stage, full review checks only stage completion, confirmations are not bound to an immutable Candidate digest, Candidate materialization occurs only during activation, the Session schema does not persist the full checklist evidence, and Active replacement plus Session save are not one transaction.
observedIssues.decision: Do not overclaim runtime enforcement in WI-10. Require manual STOP, persisted Session ID/path/SHA-256 review, no unknowns, schema-supported evidence locations, separate bounded activation approval, and explicit STOP on Active/Session mismatch; implement machine enforcement and transactional recovery in a separate corrective.
observedIssues.resolution: The three guides expose these limitations and the documentation checker rejects omission of the runtime, persistence, and atomicity boundaries.
observedIssues.followUp: In the process-issues stage, make unknown block readiness/activation, bind confirmations to Candidate revision/digest, add a schema-supported full-checklist evidence location, provide transactional rollback or equivalent recovery across Active and Session persistence, add all-unknown, stale-confirmation, Candidate-change, and Session-save-failure regressions, and complete PR/merge/closure/cleanup before release.

observedIssues.decision: WI-10 must not claim the explicit -f entrypoint works for every target. Require separately reviewed Make integration before composite lifecycle targets and record runtime entrypoint propagation as a later release-blocking process corrective.
observedIssues.resolution: The three guides and metadata checker enforce the composite-target boundary; runtime propagation is deferred to the process-issues stage.
